questions.q: Octan-1-ol is treated with PDC in DMF. The product is:
questions.explain: In DMF, PDC is a stronger oxidant and takes a saturated 1° alcohol to the carboxylic acid. In CH₂Cl₂ the same reagent stops at octanal, so the solvent decides.

questions.q: Benzyl alcohol is treated with PDC in DMF. The product is:
questions.explain: Even in DMF, allylic and benzylic primary alcohols stop at the aldehyde; only saturated 1° alcohols are taken on to acids. Choosing benzoic acid is the trap.

questions.q: Why is PDC preferred over PCC for oxidising an alcohol that also carries an acid-sensitive acetal group?
options: PDC is a Cr(III) reagent and therefore milder
PDC does not form a chromate ester
PDC is nearly neutral, while PCC is slightly acidic
questions.explain: PDC is only slightly acidic (from the pyridinium ion), so acid-sensitive groups such as acetals and silyl ethers survive. Both are Cr(VI) salts that act through chromate esters.

questions.q: Which statement about PDC is INCORRECT?
options: Its formula is (C₅H₅NH⁺)₂Cr₂O₇²⁻, with two Cr atoms bridged by O
It is prepared by adding pyridine to CrO₃ dissolved in concentrated HCl
It is only sparingly soluble in CH₂Cl₂ and is used there as a suspension
It does not oxidise tertiary alcohols
questions.explain: PDC is made by adding aqueous CrO₃ to pyridine with cooling; the CrO₃/HCl/pyridine route gives PCC, which has one Cr and a Cl.
